# DuckHaven

> DuckHaven is a self-hosted data lakehouse. Apache Iceberg brought the table format,
> Apache Polaris the catalog, and DuckDB the engine; DuckHaven is the control plane that
> holds the three together, so a team can run its own lakehouse instead of renting one.
> It gives collaborative browser worksheets, a governed Iceberg catalog, compute that
> scales to zero between runs, scheduled queries, column-level lineage, a semantic layer,
> an advisory maintenance scanner, single sign-on, fine-grained access grants, machine
> identities, and governed AI access — all on your own infrastructure, in one Docker
> Compose deploy. No cloud warehouse lock-in, no Kubernetes, no platform team required.

## Get started

- [What is DuckHaven?](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/what-is-duckhaven/): DuckHaven is a self-hosted data lakehouse.
- [Quickstart](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/quickstart/): Install DuckHaven with Docker Compose, create the first admin, and query a table you created yourself in about fifteen minutes.
- [Command line (dh)](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/cli-quickstart/): Install dh, DuckHaven's command-line interface, sign in, and run queries and catalog commands from a terminal or a script.
- [How DuckHaven works](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/how-duckhaven-works/): DuckHaven splits into a control plane that decides what may run and agents that run it, with your tables on object storage you own.

## Querying

- [Query execution](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/query-execution/): A query is checked by the API, sent to an agent, waits until the agent has memory to start it, runs, and is kept as a result file read a page at a time.
- [Run queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/run-queries/): Write SQL in a worksheet, run it on an agent you choose, read the result, and find earlier runs in History.
- [Saved queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/saved-queries/): Save a worksheet's SQL under a name so everyone in the workspace can open it, run it and schedule it.
- [Schedule queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/schedule-queries/): Run a saved query automatically on a cron schedule, such as every night at 02:00, with every run recorded.
- [Read query profiles](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/query-profiles/): Open a query's profile to see where its time and memory went, and whether it was slow because it waited or because it worked.
- [Result cache](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/result-cache/): The result cache answers a repeated query from an earlier run's result when nothing it reads has changed, so it does not run again.
- [SQL sessions](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/sql-sessions/): A SQL session is a database connection that DuckHaven holds open on one agent, so a tool can run many statements that share state.
- [Connect dbt](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/connect-dbt/): Run a dbt project on DuckHaven with the dbt-duckhaven adapter, so models build in your catalogs on DuckHaven's agents.
- [Load data with dlt](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/load-data-with-dlt/): Load data from any dlt source into DuckHaven tables with the dlt-duckhaven destination.
- [Read the session audit trail](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/session-audit/): Use the Connections screen to see which SQL sessions are holding agents, what a dbt or dlt run did, and why a session ended.
- [Troubleshoot queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/querying/troubleshooting/): Find the message you see in the results pane, in History, or in a tool's error, then follow what to do.

## Data & storage

- [Catalogs](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/catalogs/): A catalog is a collection of schemas and tables with its own metadata store and storage, which any number of workspaces can attach.
- [Manage catalogs](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/manage-catalogs/): Browse a workspace's catalogs, create, attach, detach and drop catalogs, and create and drop their schemas and tables.
- [Tables & Iceberg](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/tables/): A table in an Iceberg catalog is an Apache Iceberg table that Polaris manages, with snapshots, schema evolution and time travel.
- [Snapshots & time travel](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/snapshots-time-travel/): Browse a table's snapshot history and query the table as it was at an earlier snapshot or time.
- [DuckLake](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/ducklake/): A DuckLake catalog keeps its metadata in PostgreSQL and its data as Parquet in object storage; only DuckDB can read it, but DuckHaven can maintain it.
- [Create a DuckLake catalog](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/create-a-ducklake-catalog/): Create a DuckLake catalog, create and query its tables, and drop it when you are done with it.
- [Storage backends](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/storage-backends/): A storage backend is an object-storage location, such as a bucket and prefix, where the tables of one or more catalogs live.
- [Configure storage](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/configure-storage/): Register an AWS S3 or Azure ADLS Gen2 bucket as a storage backend, test it, and create catalogs on it.
- [Migrate a catalog's storage](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/migrate-catalog-storage/): Move a catalog to another storage backend, such as from the bundled object store to an S3 bucket, with all its data and snapshot history.
- [Lakehouse maintenance](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/data/maintenance/): The maintenance advisor scans every table, scores its health, and recommends compaction, snapshot expiry and cleanup; for DuckLake tables it can also run them.

## Metadata & lineage

- [Metadata](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/metadata/table-metadata/): What Polaris owns, what Postgres owns, and the table-metadata sidecar.
- [Lineage](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/metadata/lineage/): Where a table's data came from, and what breaks if you change it.
- [Import lineage from dbt](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/metadata/import-dbt-lineage/): Publish a dbt project's DAG into DuckHaven's lineage graph.
- [Semantic layer](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/metadata/semantic-layer/): Recording what a business term means so a metric is computed one agreed way.
- [Define metrics](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/metadata/define-metrics/): Author a semantic model and publish it so the assistant will use it.
- [Import semantics from dbt](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/metadata/import-dbt-semantics/): Import metric definitions from dbt's semantic layer.

## AI assistant & MCP

- [AI assistant](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/ai/assistant/): The governed AI data assistant and how it enforces access.
- [Use the AI assistant](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/ai/use-the-assistant/): Browse the catalog, run SQL, and propose worksheet edits with the assistant.
- [MCP server](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/ai/mcp-server/): Connecting an AI agent you already use — Claude Code, Cursor — to your data.
- [Connect an MCP client](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/ai/connect-mcp-client/): Point Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor at DuckHaven over MCP.

## Access

- [How access works](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/how-access-works/): DuckHaven decides what you can do in four independent layers, and a request is allowed only if it clears every layer that applies to it.
- [Scoped access](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/scoped-access/): A scoped catalog shows each workspace member only the schemas and tables a grant gives them, down to a single table, instead of applying their workspace role to everything.
- [Agent access](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/agent-access/): Agent access decides who may run work on an agent and who may restart or administer it, so a team can reserve compute while the rest of the fleet stays open.
- [Workspaces](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/workspaces/): A workspace is where a team works: its members and their roles, the catalogs it uses, and the worksheets, saved queries and history of everything run in it.
- [Manage users & access](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/manage-users/): Add people to DuckHaven, give them a global role, and give them a role in the workspaces they work in.
- [Service accounts & tokens](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/service-accounts/): Create a service account, give it access to a workspace, and call the API with its token, for CI pipelines, schedulers and other unattended clients.
- [Connect an IdP (SSO)](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/connect-idp/): Let people sign in to DuckHaven through your OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak, Authentik, AWS Cognito or Google Workspace.
- [Connect LDAP / AD](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/connect-ldap/): Let people sign in to DuckHaven with their LDAP or Active Directory credentials on the normal login form.
- [Offboarding & break-glass](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/offboarding/): Remove someone's access cleanly when they leave, and keep a way in when your identity provider is down.
- [Troubleshoot sign-in and access](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/access/troubleshooting/): Find the message you see on the setup or login screen, in the results pane, or in an API response, then follow what to do.

## Compute

- [Agents](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/agents/): DuckDB compute agents you pick per query.
- [Add an agent](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/add-agent/): Scale compute by adding DuckDB agents.
- [Runtimes](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/runtimes/): A runtime is the DuckDB an agent runs, together with the extensions baked into its image.
- [Elastic compute](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/elastic-compute/): Provisioning agents on demand and terminating them when they go idle.
- [Elastic compute on a single Docker host](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/elastic-docker/): Enable elastic compute with the Docker backend, provisioning agents as containers on a single host.
- [Elastic compute on Azure](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/elastic-azure/): Enable elastic compute with the Azure Container Instances backend, provisioning agents in the cloud.
- [Scaling compute](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/scaling/): DuckHaven scales compute horizontally: the control plane stays small (one box) while you add agents at the edge.
- [Agent monitoring](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/compute/agent-monitoring/): An agent's Monitoring tab — live load, where its time went, the queries it ran and what they cost, CPU and memory — and exactly how each number is measured.

## Deploy

- [Docker Compose](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/install/): Deploy the full stack with Docker Compose.
- [Reverse proxy & TLS](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/reverse-proxy-tls/): Front the stack with a reverse proxy and TLS.
- [Enable DuckLake](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/ducklake/): DuckLake is a second catalog kind, available by default.
- [High availability](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/high-availability/): Run the control plane with HA Postgres and multiple API replicas.
- [Azure with Terraform](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/azure-terraform/): Deploy the whole stack to Azure as managed infrastructure, with Terraform.
- [Updating](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/updating/): Updates pull a new image and restart the stack.
- [Backup & restore](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/backup-restore/): Back up and restore DuckHaven data.

## Operate

- [Operator runbook](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/runbook/): Operational procedures for the single control-plane box plus its agents.
- [Monitoring](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/monitoring/): The query history and audit log, Prometheus metrics, starter alert rules and a Grafana dashboard.
- [Distributed tracing](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/tracing/): DuckHaven emits OpenTelemetry traces alongside the Prometheus metrics.
- [HA failover runbook](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/ha-failover/): Drills that prove the highly-available control plane survives the failures it is designed for.
- [Troubleshooting](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/troubleshooting/): Common issues and where to look.

## Reference

- [Configuration](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/configuration/): Every DuckHaven environment variable, with its default and what it changes.
- [SQL support](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/sql-support/): DuckHaven runs DuckDB SQL, checked against an allowlist before an agent runs it; statements such as ATTACH, INSTALL and SET are rejected.
- [Permissions](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/permissions/): Every global permission, workspace role, data-grant tier and agent tier in DuckHaven, and what each one allows.
- [Agent reference](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/agent-reference/): Agent configuration and behavior.
- [CLI reference](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/cli/): Every dh command, its summary and its flags.
- [REST API](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/rest-api/): DuckHaven's REST API, under /api, does everything the web UI does, so any task can be scripted with a token.
- [SQL sessions API](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/sql-sessions-api/): The endpoints a driver uses to open a SQL session, run statements in it, stage files and close it.
- [API versions](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/api-versions/): GET /api/version reports api_version, an integer that changes only when a change breaks existing API clients.
- [Errors](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/errors/): Every API error has an HTTP status and a stable error code; this page lists each code, what causes it and what to do.
- [Operator scripts](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/operator-scripts/): The helper scripts under scripts/ back up Postgres, check DuckLake catalogs, review the assistant's answers and wait for the stack to start.
